name: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple characteristic blue, compressible venous malformations on the skin
Venous malformations involving the gastrointestinal tract confirmed by endoscopy or imaging
Recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding leading to anemia
Histopathological confirmation of venous malformations if biopsy performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple characteristic cutaneous venous malformations plus gastrointestinal venous malformations with or without recurrent bleeding
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging and endoscopic findings; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple blue compressible cutaneous venous malformations
Venous malformations of the gastrointestinal tract
searchTerms: abnormal veins in stomach or intestines

common.symptomName: Iron deficiency anemia secondary to bleeding
searchTerms: low iron anemia secondary to bleeding

common.symptomName: Pain or tenderness over cutaneous lesions

common.notes: May be palpable deep venous malformations

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal obstruction due to large venous malformations
searchTerms: intestinal blockage from large vein malformations
gut obstruction due to venous lesions
digestive tract blockage by vascular malformations

occasional.symptomName: Bleeding from venous malformations in other organs (e.g., lungs, liver)
searchTerms: bleeding from venous malformations in organs
hemorrhage in lungs or liver veins
chronic fatigue due to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Localized swelling or enlargement of affected areas

searchTerms: lung blood clots from vein malformations
pulmonary embolism due to vascular lesions

imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing venous malformations in skin and soft tissues
Endoscopic visualization of venous malformations in GI tract
CT angiography for extent of visceral involvement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Histopathology showing dilated thin-walled venous channels

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mucocutaneous telangiectasias rather than venous malformations
Family history with autosomal dominant inheritance
Arteriovenous malformations rather than venous blebs
Capillary malformations (port-wine stains) and limb hypertrophy
Venous malformations usually unilateral and associated with limb overgrowth
Absence of characteristic blue rubber bleb lesions

redFlags: Severe recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding causing hemodynamic instability
Rapid enlargement or ulceration of cutaneous lesions
Signs of thrombosis or embolism related to venous malformations
references: Blei F, et al. Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome: Clinical and Pathologic Features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
Wassef M, et al. Vascular Malformations: Classification, Diagnosis, and Treatment. Pediatr Dermatol. 2015.
